findings.title: Denial cache is consulted first and not invalidated when permissions are granted, so creators can still be denied right after creating an item
findings.body: Check() now returns a cached denial before consulting the permission cache or the DB (lines 116-121). A denial is written for 30s whenever a check fails (line 153-155), keyed by user, action, name and parent folder. If a user is denied on a dashboard or folder name (for example a get attempted before creation), then creates that resource, the stale denial is served for up to 30s. The DB-requery fallback added in this PR never runs in that window, so the exact scenario the PR is meant to fix ('dashboard/folder creator can't access what they just created') can still fail. Creation paths should invalidate or bypass the denial entry, or the denial should be checked only after the permission cache miss path has been ruled out.

findings.title: Denial cache key concatenates unescaped fields, so different resources can collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins userUID, action, name and parent with '_' and no escaping. Dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct requests map to the same key. Example: (name="a_b", parent="") and (name="a", parent="b_") both produce '...._a_b_'. A denial recorded for one resource then denies access to the other for 30s, causing false denials. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or a hash/structured key.

findings.title: List serves cached permissions with no DB requery, so newly created items are missing from lists
findings.body: The PR adds a DB fallback on cache miss for Check, but List only falls back when the user's permission map is absent from the cache (lines 180-192). If the map is cached (up to 30s), a newly created dashboard or folder is missing from the List response, because the stored permission set predates it. The creator therefore cannot see the new item in listings for the TTL window, even though Check now succeeds. This inconsistency between Check and List should be either addressed or explicitly documented.

findings.title: Test setupService uses a different TTL for basicRoleCache than NewService
findings.body: NewService creates basicRoleCache with shortCacheTTL, but setupService (line 1338) uses longCacheTTL. Tests therefore exercise a configuration that production does not use. The test helper should mirror NewService.
